prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, art-direction paintover of an existing game location. Image 1 is a current in-game screenshot from the timber footbridge that leads from the Mega Park air station onto the top road of the Mega Park, a concrete skate park set into volcanic rock in the forest of an island in autumn, in the game Yorimichi. The road runs under a concrete overpass hung with an indigo seigaiha wave banner. Below and right of the overpass's concrete abutment the ground is missing where the park meets the island: flat dark grey-blue untextured triangles, the back of a rock wall and a void. Image 2 is another place in the same game and shows the art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, pale lavender-grey rocks, autumn maples and ginkgos in rust, orange and gold, dark green pines, soft green grass. Repaint image 1 from exactly the same camera and composition as the improved AFTER version: the paintover a lead environment artist makes to show the team how to blend the two maps there. The hole is filled with a natural hillside of dark forest earth and fine grey volcanic gravel that rises from the forest floor under the footbridge to the road's edge and the foot of the abutment, so the road and the abutment stand on solid ground and no wall is seen from behind. A few layered lavender-grey volcanic rocks with moss on their tops, ferns, ochre bushes and small red maples soften the joint between the concrete and the earth, fallen leaves gather in drifts, and the forest's trees close in behind. The footbridge, the road, the overpass, its banner and the abutment stay exactly as they are. Stay in the game's style with its low-poly leaf-card trees; do not turn it photoreal. No people, no UI, no labels, no text.
